headline: South Asia: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages.
- India: Ukraine strikes Russian oil refinery, train in overnight drone attacks; 2 killed.
- Western Russia: Nighttime Russian strikes on Kyiv Oblast: timber plant catches fire, warehouses, houses and cars damaged – photos.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Military personnel data exposed in breach, agency warns.
- Military Times, 18 hours ago: Military personnel data exposed in breach, agency warns.
Unauthorized users accessed files containing the personal information of U.S. military personnel, a new breach notification letter warns.
- Military Times, 17 hours ago: 8 sailors attempted suicide aboard ships from Lincoln strike group, Cao says.
Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao confirmed that eight sailors from the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group attempted suicide.
- Military Times, 18 hours ago: Nellis Air Force Base says goodbye to last A-10 Thunderbolt II.
After five decades at the Nevada base, airmen saluted its last operational A-10 Warthog as it conducted its final flight Tuesday.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
The Caribbean: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Nighttime Russian strikes on Kyiv Oblast: timber plant catches fire, warehouses, houses and cars damaged – photos.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Nighttime Russian strikes on Kyiv Oblast: timber plant catches fire, warehouses, houses and cars damaged – photos.
A Russian attack on Kyiv Oblast overnight sparked a fire at a timber-processing plant and damaged a warehouse, three houses and four cars.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Russian state news agency publishes column claiming Russia faces new "special military operation" in Lithuania.
Kremlin-aligned Russian outlet RIA Novosti published and later deleted an opinion piece threatening Lithuania with a Russian invasion and nuclear strike.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: ArcelorMittal shuts down Ukraine's largest metallurgical company following Russian attacks.
Ukraine's largest steelmaker, ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih, suspends operations following four missile attacks that killed five employees and injured 17.
- Ukrainska Pravda, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: Russian attacks caused more power cuts in six Ukrainian regions.
Russian strikes damaged energy infrastructure in Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv, Odesa and Mykolaiv Oblasts on 25 September.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Kosovo Marks Banjska Attack Anniversary as Main Suspects Remain Free.
- Balkan Insight, 21 hours ago: Kosovo Marks Banjska Attack Anniversary as Main Suspects Remain Free.
Politicians and relatives paid tribute to Kosovo police officer killed in September 2023 Banjska attack by an armed Serb gang, while the majority of the suspects remain at liberty, most likely in Serbia.
- Politico Europe, 7 hours ago: Deutschland und Spanien zetteln Papierkrieg zu „Made in Europe“-Auslegung an.
Berlin strebt einen breit aufgestellten Verbund von Handelspartnern an, während Madrid ein gestaffeltes System vorschlägt, bei dem in der EU hergestellte Waren Vorrang genießen.
- Politico Europe, 13 hours ago: Europe grudgingly, gingerly moves toward Trump’s Board of Peace.
The European Commission is working with Trump’s body in Gaza for lack of better options. But the Board of Peace’s concrete results are slim.
- Balkan Insight, 20 hours ago: Bosnia Dismisses Two Soldiers for Glorifying Ratko Mladic.
Defence Ministry terminates contracts of two soldiers who honoured the legacy of convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Ethiopia: Ethiopia - Renewed Tigray Fighting Shows Need to Protect Civilians.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, Africanews, 6 hours ago: Ethiopia: Ethiopia - Renewed Tigray Fighting Shows Need to Protect Civilians.
[HRW] Nairobi -- Fighting in Ethiopia's northern Tigray, Amhara, and Afar regions erupted on September 22, 2026, between the Ethiopian military and forces aligned with the Tigrayan People's Liberation Front, Tigray's main political party. This follows reported clashes and airstrikes in Tigray since August, including in Tigray's regional capital, Mekelle.
- Africanews, 20 hours ago: Fighting intensifies in northern Ethiopia as Tigray rebels declare full-blown war.
Ethiopia’s army says its forces have killed 272 Tigrayan fighters and wounded 260 during a counter-offensive in Amhara. The press says the figures could not be independently verified.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 22 hours ago: Ethiopia: Attack By Rebel Group Raises Fear of Renewed War in Ethiopia.
[Premium Times] Months of rising tension in Ethiopia have now escalated into renewed armed clashes in the northern Tigray region, raising concerns that the country could slide back into a civil war.
- Africanews, one day ago: Ethiopia's federalism dilemma: Why regional power keeps fuelling conflict.
Tigrayan authorities say they are responding to attacks by federal forces, while the federal government has described the Tigrayan military action as an offensive. Both sides have accused the other of triggering the latest escalation.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Oil prices jump after Yemen’s Houthis claim attacks on Saudi facilities.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 7 hours ago: Oil prices jump after Yemen’s Houthis claim attacks on Saudi facilities.
Brent crude tops $106 a barrel after Iran-aligned rebel group claims to have successfully attacked Aramco facilities.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Israel is fighting a new war on the financial front – and it is not ready - opinion.
Settler violence has been treated as a nuisance rather than as a strategic threat that hands Israel’s adversaries ammunition on a silver platter.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: IDF chief Zamir establishes expert team to investigate drone accident that killed two soldiers.
The team, led by a Ground Forces brigadier-general, will examine the incident in order to ensure a similar one does not occur again.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Saudi Arabia allies line up support as Houthi attacks mount.
France is sending military to protect key Yanbu oil terminal; Pakistan and Turkiye to hold military talks with Riyadh.
South Africa - bottom line: Malawi: Spies On Guard - Malawi Deploys Intelligence Agents As Fertiliser Handouts Launch for 1.2million Farmers.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one hour ago: Malawi: Spies On Guard - Malawi Deploys Intelligence Agents As Fertiliser Handouts Launch for 1.2million Farmers.
[Nyasa Times] Malawi government has officially launched its 2026/27 Farm Inputs Subsidy Programme, promising more than 1.2 million smallholder farmers access to cheap fertiliser and seed -- but issued a chilling warning to officials involved in its distribution that any theft or diversion of the vital supplies will not be tolerated.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 4 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Parliament Calls for State of Emergency Over Harare Sewage Crisis.
[New Zimbabwe] Harare is facing a public health crisis as raw sewage continues to flow into rivers feeding Lake Chivero, the capital's main water source, a Parliamentary report has warned.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: Namibia: Kahungu Cruises Towards Another Term.
[Namibian] Swapo Party Women's Council (SPWC) secretary Fransina Kahungu is set to return for another five-year term after being nominated unopposed to lead the women's wing at its upcoming ninth congress.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages.
Ethiopian forces battled overnight to repel an assault by Tigray rebels in the Afar region, a humanitarian source said on Friday, with reports of an internet blackout in the north of the country. Rebels in the northern Tigray region seized local airports and launched attacks into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara this week, saying they were once again in a “full-blown war” with the federal government. Locals fear a repeat of the telecoms blackout and supplies blockade imposed on Tigray during the last civil war in 2020-2022 that killed an estimated 600,000 people.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: Security forces kill several Afghan Taliban fighters in retaliatory action along Balochistan border: sources.
Pakistani troops responded to an act of aggression along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in Balochistan and killed several Afghan Taliban on Thursday, state media reported, citing sources. State-run APP reported, citing sources, that the Afghan Taliban attempted to enter the Pakistani territory in Balochistan’s Gulistan sector and carry out an act of aggression. Meanwhile, officials also reported attacks on some border posts in Pakistan. The APP report said in retaliatory action, several Afghan Taliban fighters were killed.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: India’s theatre command push marred by capability gaps, readiness concerns.
The Modi government’s push for Integrated Theatre Commands has faced growing criticism and concerns over its implementation. The emphasis on political objectives and tight deadlines risks coming at the expense of military professionalism and could undermine the combat effectiveness of India’s armed forces across the three services. The Indian Air Force (IAF) remains the most visible victim, but critical shortages in the army and navy further expose the dangerous fragility of India’s defence posture.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Dar, Saudi and Turkish counterparts review progress on institutionalising tripartite defence pact.
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met his Saudi Arabian and Turkish counterparts on Friday to review progress on institutionalising the tripartite Makkah Defence Alliance. The agreement — signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on August 7 — empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all. Its inaugural meeting was held on Aug 31, where officials from all member states met in Istanbul to establish the institutional structure of the alliance, and Pakistan was picked to head its secretariat in Riyadh.
India - bottom line: Ukraine strikes Russian oil refinery, train in overnight drone attacks; 2 killed.
- Times of India - Top Stories, ABC News Australia, The Moscow Times, Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Ukraine strikes Russian oil refinery, train in overnight drone attacks; 2 killed.
Russian governor Yuri Slyusar said around 50 drones were destroyed over the region and the strike forced the refinery to temporarily suspend operations. He said there were no reports of casualties there. In Ulyanovsk, eight people were injured after another drone attack damaged industrial and civilian infrastructure, Governor Alexei Russkikh said. The region is home to a major electronics plant.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Hormuz To Truce Talks: Inside Iran's New '7-Day' Plan To End War.
Araghchi did not disclose whether the new proposal also addresses the nuclear questions during the proposed seven-day process.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: How AI powered autonomous drones are reshaping aerial combat.
The US Air Force is integrating Collaborative Combat Aircraft into its operational framework, enhancing aerial combat capabilities. This move aims to improve situational awareness and reduce risks to manned platforms in contested environments. The two new aircraft, General Atomics' YFQ-42A and Anduril's YFQ-44A, are currently undergoing testing. Manned-Unmanned Teaming is a key feature, allowing pilots to direct unmanned assets in combat.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Canada says it considered risk of US attack: How their militaries compare.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has raised concerns regarding the possibility of US military action against Canada under extreme circumstances. This remark comes amidst escalating trade tensions between the two nations. The stark differences in military budget and resources underline Canada's ongoing commitment to modernizing its defense capabilities and reinforcing its Arctic strategies, while both countries continue to work together under NORAD for North American defense.
Asia - bottom line: France to protect key Saudi oil terminal as Houthis step up missile attacks.
- South China Morning Post - China, 5 hours ago: France to protect key Saudi oil terminal as Houthis step up missile attacks.
President Emmanuel Macron said France would send troops to defend an oil plant in Saudi Arabia as the Iran-backed Houthi militia took responsibility for new attacks on the kingdom. Macron said in a television interview Thursday with TF1 and France 2 that he would send soldiers and military support to help protect the Saudi port of Yanbu. Saudi Arabia came under attack from the Houthi militia on Thursday, with the kingdom saying it intercepted missiles fired towards the Red Sea port of Yanbu and...
- South China Morning Post - China, just now: Why did Xi and China’s first lady bring their own flasks to White House banquet?.
Amid the polished silverware and fine crystal stemware on display at the state dinner in the White House on Thursday sat the vacuum flasks brought by Chinese President Xi Jinping and first lady Peng Liyuan. The couple’s flasks, black for Xi and white for Peng, were spotted on their table during the formal dinner, signalling a subtle self-assurance as cultural authenticity met high diplomacy. Extending this everyday practice to the White House banquet was in tune with the host nation’s own...
- South China Morning Post - China, just now: Young Chinese women sew own underwear, clothes, amid frustration with fast fashion.
Frustrated by low-quality materials, careless craftsmanship, and escalating prices, some young women in China are taking matters into their own hands by learning to sew their own underwear, accessories, and handbags. This summer, a surge of sewing enthusiasts flocked to RedNote to showcase their handmade creations. Many beginners embarked on their journey with underwear, assuming it would be a straightforward first project due to its minimal fabric requirements. However, they quickly encountered...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: Xi at White House, trade-war truce extension, Golden Week travel.
Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump discussed artificial intelligence (AI) and Taiwan at the White House on Thursday as part of a state visit dominated by pageantry. On AI, Xi said that “the right thing to do is to draw on each other’s strengths, not guard against each other”, according to a statement from the Chinese foreign ministry. He also backed continued dialogue about risks, joint efforts to prevent misuse and keeping AI under human control. Trump earlier said on...
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: Lee accuses Ukraine of violating pact by revealing North Korean POW transfer.
- NK News, South China Morning Post - China, 7 hours ago: Lee accuses Ukraine of violating pact by revealing North Korean POW transfer.
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Thursday expressed concern over Volodymyr Zelensky’s public disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) to South Korea, saying the Ukrainian president had violated an agreement to keep the move private. In a statement posted on X, Lee took aim at the Ukrainian leader […]

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Open AI attacked Australia’s health system – and then doubled down on its negligence. The time for ‘wait and see’ is over | Kate Crawford and Edward Santow.
- The Guardian - Australia, 11 hours ago: Open AI attacked Australia’s health system – and then doubled down on its negligence. The time for ‘wait and see’ is over | Kate Crawford and Edward Santow.
Human hackers face serious consequences, and so must AI companies. There is no excuse for what happened Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast When you get sick, Medicare exists to take care of you. It sits at the centre of a health system that our prime minister rightly calls the envy of the world. It’s one of the few institutions nearly every Australian still trusts. So when an AI company threatens this system, it couldn’t be more serious.
- The Guardian - Australia, one hour ago: Rogue AI hacks government system for first time – The Latest.
A government database has been hacked for the first time by a rogue OpenAI agent, which infiltrated part of the Australian healthcare scheme in June. OpenAI became aware of the hack in August, but only informed the government in September. Australia’s prime minister, Anthony Albanese, has expressed his ‘extreme concern’ about the hack, which raises serious AI security concerns for governments around the world. Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s UK technology editor Robert Booth – watch on YouTube Continue reading...
- The Guardian - Australia, 4 hours ago: Pocock calls for AI safety act after Medicare breach – as it happened.
This blog is now closed Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast AI hack of Medicare exposes Australia’s vulnerabilities Technology experts have warned revelations an artificial intelligence agent hacked Medicare’s internal systems will not be the only dangerous breach of government data and have called for Australia to boost its protections against the growing risk. Frontier AI now has capability to expose those vulnerabilities at a rate quicker than we can keep up, quicker than we can patch them.
- ABC News Australia, 5 hours ago: Fishtailing caravan captured on truckie dash cam prompts holiday warning.
Dash-cam footage captures the frightening moment a caravan begins fishtailing while overtaking a truck driver in Western Australia's Great Southern region.

This briefing is compiled automatically from regional news feeds and has not been cross-referenced by an editor. Treat single-source claims as unconfirmed. I will be back with the next update.
